html:
Sindh is the land of the lower Indus River, in today's south east Pakistan. It appears on the maps for 900 and 1800, a thousand years in which it was often a state of its own on the edge of larger empires.

After the Arab conquest of 712 it was a province of the caliphate. By the mid 800s the Arab governors of the Habbari dynasty ruled it themselves from Mansura, while Multan in the north went its own way. Later local dynasties took over:

  • the Soomras, from the 11th century to about 1351;
  • the Sammas, to 1520, with their capital at Thatta;
  • Arghun and Tarkhan rulers, then the Mughals from 1591;
  • the Kalhoras in the 1700s, and the Talpurs from 1783.

On the 1800 map the Talpur emirs rule. In 1843 Britain conquered Sindh after the Battle of Miani. Its life always depended on the Indus, which watered its fields and carried its trade to the sea.
